observation_summary: The MultidimensionalCounter.getCounts(int) method returns incorrect multidimensional indices for certain unidimensional input values, as evidenced by the test failure where index 3 resulted in [0, 2] instead of [0, 3].
reasoning_summary: The bug is a failure in the computational logic used to map a unidimensional index to a multidimensional array of indices. This is a procedural calculation error within the method responsible for the conversion, which fits the definition of Algorithm/Method. It is not a missing guard (Checking), a simple initialization error (Assignment/Initialization), or a design-level capability gap (Function/Class/Object).
evidence_used: MultidimensionalCounter.getCounts(int) returns wrong array of indices
junit.framework.AssertionFailedError: Wrong multidimensional index for [3][2] expected:<3> but was:<2>

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The issue is not a wrong constant or variable initialization, but a flaw in the mathematical procedure used to calculate the indices.
There is no evidence that a missing boundary check or condition is the root cause; the logic itself produces the wrong result.
